item.title: Lautoka families receive drinking water as community steps up relief efforts

item.content:encoded:
Families in several Lautoka communities who have been without drinking water for weeks are receiving bottled water from the Lautoka Ratepayers Association, as worsening water shortages caused by El Niño leave households struggling to meet their daily needs.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says they have been distributing drinking water to affected areas, including Saru, Tawatawa, Vuda Back Road, Wairabetia and parts of Tavakubu, with deliveries continuing today.

Reddy says each family is receiving between 12 and 16 bottles of water, with the Association receiving further requests when households run out.

He says the water is being purchased through the association's own contributions and donations from NGOs, members of the public and families in Australia.

Reddy says the demand is high as some families have gone weeks without water, while rivers they previously relied on for bathing have also dried up.

He says some residents have resorted to drinking river water, while children are also facing difficulties maintaining their hygiene.

Reddy says some school children are wearing the same uniform throughout the five-day school week because their families do not have enough water to wash their clothes.

He says some children are also missing school, while families with flush toilets are facing growing sanitation concerns due to the lack of water.

Reddy is also concerned about students sitting their Year 12 examinations, saying the lack of water and proper sanitation at schools could affect their well-being and concentration.

He says while some students are bringing drinking water to school, there are concerns about how they can wash their hands and use the toilets when there is no water available.

He is calling on the Government and the Water Authority of Fiji to install water tanks at strategic locations to make water more accessible to affected communities.

Reddy says the tanks could be placed at schools, shops and other accessible locations where residents can collect water for drinking and cooking.

He says this would allow families to access water more easily while they continue to deal with the shortages.

item.title: Police warn of tough action in child negligence cases following Wailoaloa drownings
item.description: Following the deaths of three young girls on Monday at Wailoaloa Beach in Nadi, the Fiji Police Force says it will take an aggressive approach to investigating cases where negligence may have contributed to a child's death. Police say parents and guardians have a responsibility to ensure that young children, particularly those under the age of 11, are properly supervised at all times.
item.content:encoded:
Following the deaths of three young girls on Monday at Wailoaloa Beach in Nadi, the Fiji Police Force says it will take an aggressive approach to investigating cases where negligence may have contributed to a child's death.

Police say parents and guardians have a responsibility to ensure that young children, particularly those under the age of 11, are properly supervised at all times.

They stress that negligence involving children is a serious matter and will not be taken lightly.

Police say people entrusted with the care of children have previously been charged and taken to court in cases involving negligence.

They say investigations must follow the proper legal process, with investigation files referred to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for a decision on whether charges should be laid.

The warning follows the deaths of three girls, aged 5, 7 and 8, in two separate drowning incidents at Wailoaloa Beach.

The deaths have brought Fiji's national drowning toll to 50, compared with 31 during the same period last year.

item.title: Dick Peng remains overseas as $20M tax fraud investigation continues
item.description: Dick Peng, who is linked to an alleged $20 million tax fraud case, remains out of the country as Police investigations continue. Assistant Commissioner of Police Crime Loraini Seru confirms that the Anti-Money Laundering is still investigating the matter.
item.content:encoded:
Dick Peng, who is linked to an alleged $20 million tax fraud case, remains out of the country as Police investigations continue.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Crime Loraini Seru confirms that the Anti-Money Laundering is still investigating the matter.

Peng left Fiji despite a Stop Departure Order being issued against him.

Fiji Revenue and Customs Service CEO Udit Singh had earlier confirmed that the FRCS did not remove the Stop Departure Order.

item.title: Nausori Council clears rubbish pile after Qacoya Road residents raise concerns
item.description: People living along Qacoya Road in Nausori have raised concerns about a pile of rubbish left near the roundabout, with the Nausori Town Council confirming that it was cleared this morning after being left following funeral services in the area. A concerned resident claims the rubbish was not collected yesterday, despite Council workers having piled it up near the roundabout.
item.content:encoded:
People living along Qacoya Road in Nausori have raised concerns about a pile of rubbish left near the roundabout, with the Nausori Town Council confirming that it was cleared this morning after being left following funeral services in the area.

A concerned resident claims the rubbish was not collected yesterday, despite Council workers having piled it up near the roundabout.

The resident says dogs were scattering the rubbish around the area and claims attempts to contact the Council had gone unanswered.

However, Nausori Town Council Chief Executive Officer Rajesh Kumar says the concerned resident has been warned to remove their garbage.

Kumar also says a Council team carried out an inspection of the area this morning.

We have sent further questions to Nausori Town Council.
